en.title: One week, 67,960 km² more white ground in Norway
en.description: One week, 67,960 km² more white ground in Norway. Snow cover, new snow, resorts and the days ahead in Norway on 17 November.
en.lede: Seven days ago about 183,090 km² of high ground was white in Norway; today it is 251,050 km², a gain of 67,960 km².

p: The new white ground is mostly in the middle heights, where a single cold spell can turn grass into a usable base.
The white area in Norway stands at about 251,050 km² today, little changed from yesterday. Roughly 89 % of the country's mapped mountains and hills are covered.

sections.h: How much of the country is white
p: Even the lowest ground is mostly white. A week ago it was 183,090 km², so the cover has grown by 67,960 km².
Hardangervidda and Jotunheimen got the most fresh snow over three days, up to 37 cm.
In the past day, up to 4 cm was added.
At least 5 cm fell over some 122,420 km².

sections.h: The resorts with the most snow
p: The deepest snow of the country's resorts is at Riksgränsen: 171 cm.
Next on the list: Sulitjelma Fjellandsby (127 cm), Tromsø Alpinpark (91 cm), Steilia (60 cm) and Galdhøpiggen Sommerskisenter (59 cm).
At Riksgränsen: 3 cm of fresh snow over three days, 5 cm more expected by Friday 20 November.
At Sulitjelma Fjellandsby: 8 cm of fresh snow over three days, 5 cm more expected by Friday 20 November.
Snow lies on the upper slopes of 141 out of 155 resorts in Norway.

The rest of the shortlist: Tromsø Alpinpark: 91 cm on top, 10 cm in three days, 3 cm expected; Steilia: 60 cm on top, 3 cm in three days, 2 cm expected; Galdhøpiggen Sommerskisenter: 59 cm on top, 12 cm in three days, 6 cm expected.
Expect up to 19 cm on the snowiest slopes by the third day; the seven-day total reaches 39 cm.
The snowiest day looks like Friday 20 November, with up to 16 cm in the snowiest spots.

sections.h: How deep it is, height by height
p: By height, the picture looks like this: 0-500 m: on average 7 cm (80 % of the ground white); 500-1,000 m: on average 18 cm (96 % of the ground white); 1,000-1,500 m: on average 24 cm (100 % of the ground white); 1,500-2,000 m: on average 28 cm (100 % of the ground white); 2,000-2,500 m: on average 38 cm (100 % of the ground white).

Resort by resort, today against a normal 17 November: Riksgränsen: 54 cm at about 708 m, against 59 cm in a normal year; Sulitjelma Fjellandsby: 49 cm at about 465 m, against 52 cm in a normal year; Tromsø Alpinpark: 17 cm at about 222 m, against 37 cm in a normal year; Steilia: 30 cm at about 455 m, against 56 cm in a normal year.
0 of these 4 resorts are above their usual depth for the date.
These depths are for one height on each mountain, below the top, so they read lower than the upper-slope numbers further down.
In past winters the best snow at Riksgränsen usually came early April / mid-April.

For comparison, the neighbours on the same day: Sweden: 79 % white, deepest Björkliden with 131 cm, up to 17 cm in the week ahead; Finland: 59 % white, deepest Kallin with 25 cm, up to 15 cm in the week ahead.

sections.h: Planning a day on the snow
p: Above 0 m the ground is almost fully white (80 % covered), so runs up there have a continuous base.
If you can choose the day, go after Friday 20 November: the fresh snow then has time to settle and the roads to be cleared.
Fresh snow on top of the base means soft turns on the upper slopes, while the lower runs stay patchy.
With more snow in the forecast, the next days should improve things further.

advice: Check the resort's own lift status before you travel.
Early-season snow is thin over rocks: ski the groomed runs first.
Snow above the tree line can be wind-packed: watch the ridges.

nb.title: Snøforhold i Norge, 17. november 2026: skisteder, nysnø og de neste dagene
nb.description: Snø i Norge 17. november: snødekke, nysnø, snødybde etter høyde, de neste dagene og de beste skistedene.
nb.lede: Tirsdag 17. november: snøen dekker rundt 251 050 km² i Norge. Arealet er nesten det samme som i går. Det er 89 % av området i Norge vi følger.

p: Snøen ligger helt ned til lavlandet og kysten. Sammenlignet med 183 090 km² for sju dager siden er det 67 960 km² mer.
På tre døgn kom mest nysnø her: Hardangervidda og Jotunheimen (opptil 37 cm).
Bare det siste døgnet kom det opptil 4 cm.

Snødybden avhenger av høyden: 0–500 m: i snitt 7 cm (80 % snødekt); 500–1 000 m: i snitt 18 cm (96 % snødekt); 1 000–1 500 m: i snitt 24 cm (100 % snødekt); 1 500–2 000 m: i snitt 28 cm (100 % snødekt); 2 000–2 500 m: i snitt 38 cm (100 % snødekt).
Nysnø oppå grunnlaget gir myke svinger øverst; lenger ned er det flekkete.
Uka kan gi opptil 39 cm, hvorav opptil 19 cm de neste tre dagene.
Den snørikeste dagen: fredag, 20. november, opptil 16 cm.
Mest snø i de øvre bakkene: Riksgränsen, 171 cm.
Deretter: Sulitjelma Fjellandsby (127 cm), Tromsø Alpinpark (91 cm), Steilia (60 cm) og Galdhøpiggen Sommerskisenter (59 cm).
Sulitjelma Fjellandsby: 8 cm nysnø på tre dager og opptil 5 cm til innen fredag, 20. november.

advice: Sjekk at heisene går før du drar.
Tidlig i sesongen er snøen tynn over steinene: hold deg i preparerte bakker.
